title: Marked equivalence-arrow endpoint fibration
statement:
Use quasicategories, full coherent functor categories and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and marked simplicial sets, internal Homs, natural and sharp markings and the marked cartesian model structure of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. For any small quasicategory $C$, put $W=(C^
atural)^{(\Delta^1)^\sharp}$ and let $V$ be its underlying simplicial set. Then $V$ is the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)$ on equivalence edges, and $W=V^
atural$. The endpoint map $W	o C^
atural	imes C^
atural$ is a model fibration. These constructions are natural in $C$ and valid in every input universe, including for empty $C$.

source.place: HTT Section 3.1.3 internal marked Hom, Proposition 3.1.4.1, and Corollary 3.1.4.3. Agent-formulated marked endpoint-fibration consequence of the pushout-product lifting axiom; source read online on 2026-10-17. No Stacks tag states this marked-quasicategory result.

proof.text: Put $I=(\Delta^1)^\sharp$ and $X=C^\natural$. By the marked internal-Hom adjunction of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], an $n$-simplex of the underlying simplicial set $V$ is a marked map $(\Delta^n)^\flat\times I\to X$. Indeed maps $(\Delta^n)^\flat\to W$ are exactly underlying simplicial maps $\Delta^n\to V$: the flat marking adds no condition since simplicial maps preserve degenerate edges. An edge of $(\Delta^n)^\flat\times I$ is marked exactly when its first coordinate is degenerate. Thus a simplicial map $h:\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to C$ defines such a marked map if and only if, for every vertex $a\in\Delta^n$, its vertical edge $h|_{\{a\}\times\Delta^1}$ is an equivalence; the remaining marked edges are degenerate and already map to marked edges. After interchanging the two factors, $h$ is an $n$-simplex of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)$ whose vertices are equivalence edges. This condition is preserved by all simplicial operators, since restriction sends vertices to vertices. The full-subcategory definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] therefore identifies $V$ with exactly the asserted full simplicial subset.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, opening internal-Hom adjunction and the formula for its underlying simplicial set (printed p. 154); explicit simplex calculation.

proof.text: Let $B=(\partial\Delta^1)^\sharp$. Its simplices are the two constant simplices in each degree, and its only edges are degenerate. The inclusion $i:B\hookrightarrow I$ is injective on simplices, hence a cofibration by [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. For every marked simplicial set $T$, the product $T\times B$ is the disjoint union of two copies of $T$, with the original marking on each copy: a product edge is marked just when its $T$ coordinate is marked. Consequently a marked map $T\times B\to X$ is exactly a pair of marked maps $T\to X$. The internal-Hom adjunction identifies $X^B$ with $X\times X$. Under this identification restriction $q:X^I\to X^B$ is evaluation at the two endpoints, including on markings, since its transpose restricts the evaluation map to $B$.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, internal-Hom adjunction; boundary of the interval and evaluation.

proof.text: To prove that $q$ is a model fibration, fix a trivial cofibration $j:T\to T'$ and a commutative square with left side $j$, right side $q$, top map $a:T\to X^I$, and bottom map $b:T'\to X^B$. Transposition gives $\widetilde a:T\times I\to X$ and $\widetilde b:T'\times B\to X$, agreeing on $T\times B$ by the square equation. Their pushout therefore gives a marked map $P=(T'\times B)\amalg_{T\times B}(T\times I)\to X$. The map $k:P\to T'\times I$ is the pushout product $j\mathbin{\square}i$. The cartesian pushout-product assertion of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model] says that $k$ is a trivial cofibration, since $i$ is a cofibration and $j$ is trivial. The same node says $X=C^\natural$ is fibrant, so the map $P\to X$ extends to $H:T'\times I\to X$ by the lifting characterization of $X\to *$. Transposing $H$ gives $\ell:T'\to X^I$ with $\ell j=a$ and $q\ell=b$, because $H$ restricts to the two given maps. This solves every such square, precisely the node's characterization of a model fibration.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.4.3 (printed pp. 161-162), applied to j and the marked interval boundary; Proposition 3.1.4.1 for fibrancy of C-natural.

proof.text: We also verify fibrancy of the exponent, rather than assuming its marking is natural. For either of the two marked objects $J=(\Delta^1)^\sharp$ and $J=(\Delta^1)^\flat$, the map $\varnothing\to J$ is a cofibration by [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. Given a trivial cofibration $j:T\to T'$ and a marked map $T\to X^J$, transpose it to $T\times J\to X$. The pushout product of $j$ with $\varnothing\to J$ is $T\times J\to T'\times J$, since all products with the empty object are empty. It is a trivial cofibration by the same cited axiom. Fibrancy of $X$ extends the transposed map to $T'\times J$, whose transpose is the required extension to $T'\to X^J$. Hence $X^J$ is fibrant. The cited fibrant-object characterization says its underlying simplicial set is a quasicategory and its marking consists exactly of the equivalences. For $J=(\Delta^1)^\sharp$, the underlying set is $V$ by Step 1, so this gives $W=V^\natural$. For $J=(\Delta^1)^\flat$, the product $(\Delta^n)^\flat\times J$ marks only degenerate edges, so the underlying set of $X^J$ is all of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)$. This also checks that the ambient functor simplicial set in the full-subcategory assertion is a quasicategory.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.4.3 with the empty-to-interval cofibration, and Proposition 3.1.4.1; both markings of the interval treated explicitly.

proof.text:
For a simplicial functor $F:C	o D$, applying $F$ to an inverse edge and its two inverse-triangle witnesses proves directly that $F$ preserves equivalence edges, using [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Thus it defines a marked map $F^
atural:C^
atural	o D^
atural$. Postcomposition on the marked internal Homs gives $W_C	o W_D$. The simplex description in Step 1 sends $h$ to $Fh$, so it is the usual restriction of postcomposition to equivalence arrows; endpoint evaluation commutes with it by restriction of $Fh$. Identities and composites obey the same equations. All products and markings used here are formed from simplices of $C$, finite standard simplices, and subsets or function sets between small sets. They remain in the input universe; the model axiom and fibrant-object characterization are available in that universe and stable under enlargement by [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. If $C$ is empty, there are no maps $\Delta^n	imes\Delta^1	o C$ in any degree, so $V$ and $W$ are empty, as is the endpoint target. The lifting arguments above still apply, without a vertex or nonemptiness choice. This includes the required empty case.

source.place: Functoriality of the adjunction and degreewise descriptions; the universe-relative point model of the cited node. Empty input checked directly.

The required model-theoretic assertions are taken from lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model. HTT is not archived in literature/; WANTED in report.md.

lean.statement: theorem equivalence_arrow_path_object (C : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory C] : (∃ e : (equivalenceArrowFunctor.obj (natural C)).underlying ≅ (Enhanced.equivalenceDiagrams (Δ[1] : SSet.{u}) C).toSSet, ∀ (n m : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (h : (equivalenceArrowFunctor.obj (natural C)).underlying.obj n) (a : n ⟶ m) (x : (Δ[1] : SSet.{u}).obj m), ((e.hom.app n h).val.app m a) x = h.val.app m (x, stdSimplex.objEquiv.symm a.unop)) ∧ equivalenceArrowFunctor.obj (natural C) = natural (equivalenceArrowFunctor.obj (natural C)).underlying ∧ (cof ⊓ weak).rlp (equivalenceArrowEndpoints (natural C)) ∧ (∀ (D : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory D] (F : C ⟶ D), ∃ f : natural C ⟶ natural D, f.val = F ∧ equivalenceArrowFunctor.map f ≫ equivalenceArrowEndpoints (natural D) = equivalenceArrowEndpoints (natural C) ≫ productMap f f)
